channel.title: Frontier Wire
channel.description: AI news: frontier labs, research, policy and commentary.

item.title: IndiaAI Mission unveils three indigenous AI foundation models
item.description: The IndiaAI Mission released three domestically developed foundation models—EKA‑1 by Soket AI Labs and Dhīr 2B and Dhīr 5B by ZenteiQ AiTech Innovations—at a New Delhi event on Nov 3. EKA‑1 is a 26.3‑billion‑parameter model supporting 22 Indian languages, while the Dhīr models are open‑source multilingual assistants designed for on‑premise and offline use. The models provide India with locally tailored AI capabilities and the ability to run AI securely without cloud connectivity.

item.title: Google lets schools enable Gemini, NotebookLM and Search separately after backlash
item.description: Google announced that schools can choose to enable Gemini, Gemini Notebook (NotebookLM), and Search individually. Administrators who block AI tools will also lose access to Google Search. The decision ties AI features to core search, forcing schools to adopt Google’s AI suite to retain search functionality.

item.title: Cat Wu and Thariq Shihipar leave Anthropic product team for Claude Code
item.description: Cat Wu, head of product for Claude Code and Cowork, announced on Nov 3 2026 that she is leaving Anthropic after two years; Thariq Shihipar, who also worked on Claude Code, announced his departure the month before. The leadership changes occur as Anthropic readies a major IPO, prompting scrutiny of the future direction of its Claude Code coding assistant.

item.title: Traversal raises $120 million at $1 billion valuation to expand AI‑driven site reliability engineering
item.description: Traversal announced a $120 million Series B funding round co‑led by Kleiner Perkins, Redpoint Ventures and Khosla Ventures, valuing the company at $1 billion. The AI‑agent platform is used by firms such as American Express, PepsiCo, Nubank and DigitalOcean to automate incident investigation and other SRE tasks. The funding underscores growing investor confidence that AI agents can reduce costly downtime by automating complex site‑reliability operations.

item.title: Revolut cuts AI coding inference costs by about 90% with self‑hosted GLM
item.description: Revolut reduced its AI coding inference spend to roughly one‑tenth of prior costs by self‑hosting open‑weight GLM models from Z.ai on its own NVIDIA GPUs. The change improved engineering lead time by 70% and coding time by 60% for about 2,000 engineers. It shows how large fintechs can lower AI operating expenses and speed development by moving to open‑source models.

item.title: Anthropic releases FlashProve to cryptographically verify AI model responses
item.description: Anthropic unveiled FlashProve, an open‑source prototype that generates cryptographic proofs showing a language‑model reply came from a specific set of weights. The system runs at about 110 tokens per second on Meta’s Llama 4 Maverick, with proofs around 19 MB that a CPU can check in 17‑21 seconds. It gives AI users a way to confirm the model that generated a response, addressing concerns about hidden model swapping in AI services.

item.title: Apple opens Siri AI to all developers via App Intents in iOS 27.3 beta
item.description: Apple announced that developers can integrate Siri AI into any iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and visionOS app using App Intents, starting with the iOS 27.3 beta. The preview lets apps expose content and actions for natural‑language requests without naming the app. It expands Siri AI’s reach, letting third‑party apps perform tasks via voice, which could increase user engagement and drive AI adoption on Apple devices.

item.title: AI inference startup Fal valued at $16B after $1.3B funding round
item.description: Fal, a San Francisco AI inference startup, raised $1.3 billion in a Series F round led by Bessemer Venture Partners, valuing the company at $16 billion after reporting $800 million in annualized revenue. The deal highlights the rapid growth and high demand for AI inference services that run trained models for customers.

item.title: Meta targets at least $20 billion in cross‑border bond offering, debuting euro tranche
item.description: Meta Platforms is preparing a cross‑border investment‑grade bond sale that could raise at least $20 billion, including its first euro‑denominated tranche and its first major debt transaction in six months. Citigroup and Morgan Stanley will host investor calls as the company seeks funding for AI and data‑center expansion. The financing will provide Meta with capital to fund its AI and data‑center projects, while giving investors a new high‑grade bond option in both dollars and euros.

item.title: StateBench benchmark reveals transformers struggle with long-context state tracking
item.description: AllenAI introduced StateBench, a benchmark that measures how well language models track entity states over long documents. Tests show recurrent and hybrid models outperform frontier transformer models such as Gemini 3.8 Flash, Claude Opus 5.5, and GPT-6 Sol and Luna on harder state‑tracking tasks. Accurate state tracking is essential for applications like code analysis and narrative understanding, highlighting current limits of leading AI models.

item.title: Anthropic compute costs rise to 58% of revenue in Q3, widening operating loss
item.description: Anthropic reported Q3 revenue of $17 billion, up from $11.5 billion in the prior quarter. Compute spending rose to $10 billion, or 58% of revenue, widening its operating loss. High compute costs highlight the financial challenges of scaling AI models for investors and the broader AI market.

item.title: Google Antigravity AI accelerates antimicrobial peptide discovery
item.description: DeepMind announced that its agentic cheminformatics system, Google Antigravity, is being used to speed the search for antimicrobial peptides, according to a Science article in October 2026. The tool could help identify new antibiotics faster, addressing growing antimicrobial resistance.

item.title: Google disables Search for schools that reject its AI tools
item.description: Google will turn off Search for K‑12 accounts unless administrators enable its Gemini AI suite, meaning schools that block AI lose web search access. The policy links core internet search to AI, forcing educators to choose between AI tools and basic search functionality.

item.title: Simon Willison shows Qwen 3.8 27B can interpret raw model weights
item.description: Simon Willison reported that the Qwen 3.8 27B model running on his laptop was able to read and reason about raw neural network weights. The experiment took about 45 minutes and reproduced results described in the paper on Weight‑Space Programming. It shows that large language models can analyze and potentially modify model parameters without external code, opening new avenues for model debugging and self‑optimization.

item.title: AI accelerates semiconductor fab simulations up to 35x
item.description: AI is transforming semiconductor manufacturing by speeding up simulations and enabling digital twins, allowing engineers to evaluate more alternatives before physical trials. NVIDIA’s cuDSS and PhysicsNeMo libraries deliver up to 35× faster multiphysics simulations for Applied Materials and up to 17× acceleration for Siemens lithography software. Faster, more accurate simulations let chip makers cut development cycles and improve yield, affecting the supply of advanced chips.

item.title: CrowdStrike to acquire Fiddler AI for $400 million and Dreadnode for $95 million
item.description: CrowdStrike announced agreements to buy AI‑agent observability firm Fiddler AI and AI‑security testing startup Dreadnode, in deals reported at roughly $400 million and $95 million respectively, paid mostly in cash. The acquisitions will be integrated into CrowdStrike’s Falcon platform as Falcon Observe and expanded testing capabilities. The moves give security vendors tools to monitor, explain and control AI agents, addressing emerging risks as companies deploy them faster than traditional security can keep up.

item.title: Baidu launches Apollo World AI system to simulate up to 100,000 km of robotaxi driving daily
item.description: Baidu introduced Apollo World, an AI system that can generate up to 100,000 km of simulated driving each day, and is already being used to train its Apollo Go robotaxi fleet. The system lets autonomous‑vehicle developers train and test self‑driving software in a virtual environment, lowering the cost and time needed for real‑world road testing.

item.title: EU court adviser says Google’s Gemini may infringe press copyright
item.description: An advocate general of the EU’s top court warned that Google’s Gemini chatbot could breach copyright when it reproduces press articles, especially if it bypasses paywalls or copies the expression of the text. Training on copyrighted material is allowed under the text‑and‑data‑mining exception, but using that material to answer users may not be. The ruling could shape how AI chatbots handle copyrighted news content across Europe.

item.title: NVIDIA expands physical and agentic AI services to cities worldwide
item.description: NVIDIA and partners are deploying physical AI, agentic AI and digital twins in cities across Europe, Asia and the United States, using shared computing infrastructure to let local governments run AI locally. Projects include resident‑service bots in Madrid, vision agents in Poland and traffic‑management agents in Malaysia that aim to support over 17,000 cameras by 2027. The deployments show how cities can use AI for public services while keeping data under local control.

item.title: India becomes ChatGPT’s largest market by weekly active users, base doubles since Jan 2026
item.description: OpenAI says India now has the highest weekly active user count for ChatGPT worldwide, with the local user base having doubled since January 2026. The company is expanding local computing capacity, Indian-language features and Android‑first products, and plans UPI‑related announcements. The growth shows how rapidly AI adoption is scaling in emerging markets, influencing product strategy and infrastructure investment.

item.title: MIT researchers show LLMs can read and edit neural network weights without retraining
item.description: MIT’s CSAIL team demonstrated that a large language model (GPT‑6 Astra) can examine and modify a neural network’s weights directly, improving a small language model by changing only 0.016% of its parameters. In experiments the model raised the MATH‑500 score from 7.9% to 48.1% and GSM8K from 13.8% to 67.1%. It shows a way to fix or enhance AI models without costly retraining, opening new debugging and optimization pathways.

item.title: PowerUp Money raises $10 million to expand AI‑led wealth management in India
item.description: PowerUp Money secured $10 million in a round led by Flourish Ventures and will use the funds to develop its AI‑powered wealth advisory platform and expand its managed advisory service Infinite. The Bengaluru startup, with over 1.5 million users and 1 lakh paid Elite members, says Infinite has amassed nearly Rs 500 crore AUM. The investment shows AI is being used to deliver more comprehensive, personalized digital wealth management at lower cost, a trend relevant to AI followers.

item.title: Huawei says Ascend 960DT AI chip will use Samsung and SK Hynix HBM
item.description: Huawei told some customers that a large share of its upcoming flagship AI chip, Ascend 960DT, will be equipped with high‑bandwidth memory from Samsung and SK Hynix, which is being smuggled into China via board‑packaging loopholes. It shows how U.S. export controls are being bypassed and that Chinese AI hardware still depends on foreign memory components.

item.title: Anthropic reports 1,100% revenue surge ahead of IPO, commits $895B to compute
item.description: Anthropic said quarterly revenue jumped to $17 billion, a 1,100% increase year‑over‑year. It also pledged roughly $895 billion in spending on computing, including $70 billion due before September 2027, as it prepares for a Wall Street listing later this month. The figures show the scale of capital required to train large AI models and test investor appetite for an AI‑focused public company.

item.title: Salesforce to acquire Cresta for $2.7 billion
item.description: Salesforce announced a definitive agreement to buy Cresta, an AI‑powered contact‑center automation provider, for $2.7 billion. The deal is slated to close in the first quarter of Salesforce’s fiscal 2028, pending regulatory approval. The acquisition adds voice‑first AI automation to Salesforce’s Service Cloud, expanding AI capabilities for customer‑service teams.

item.title: Trajectory raises $45 million Series A to automate AI model post‑training
item.description: Trajectory, a startup founded by three Stanford alumni, announced a $45 million Series A round at a $300 million valuation, led by Sequoia with participation from Nvidia, Bessemer and Bain Capital. The company’s platform lets non‑technical users continuously fine‑tune open‑source models through feedback‑driven continual learning. It lowers the technical barrier and cost for businesses to adapt AI models to specialized tasks, speeding wider AI adoption.

item.title: Anthropic open-sources FlashProve for provable inference on Llama 4 Maverick
item.description: Anthropic released an open‑source prototype called FlashProve that can cryptographically prove a response came from a specified model. On a single H100 GPU it generates proofs for the 400‑billion‑parameter Llama 4 Maverick at about 110 tokens per second, with proof files around 19 MB per 1,024‑token request. It gives users a way to verify that AI outputs are produced by the model they expect, addressing trust and compliance concerns.

item.title: GPT-6 Astra edits 0.016% of Qwen3.5-0.8B weights, boosting math performance sixfold
item.description: Researchers used GPT-6 Astra to edit the weights of the Qwen3.5-0.8B language model. The edit changed 0.016% of the weights and reportedly improved math reasoning up to six times and instruction following three times, without gradients or additional training. It shows that large language models can be refined by directly modifying a tiny portion of their parameters, potentially reducing the cost of model improvement.

item.title: Anthropic adds rule to stop Claude Code from cloning existing video games
item.description: Anthropic updated Claude Code’s system prompt to forbid recreating specific games, adding a rule that allows only original or genre‑based games. The change was first spotted on Oct 27 and confirmed by engineer Addy Osmani. It aims to protect game developers’ intellectual property and limit AI‑driven game cloning.

item.title: OpenAI raises security bug bounty rewards and adds new researcher bonuses
item.description: OpenAI announced increased bug bounty payouts and introduced report quality, loyalty, and priority campaign bonuses for independent security researchers. The move aims to boost incentives for finding vulnerabilities in OpenAI’s AI systems, enhancing overall safety.
